content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The draft specification is ready for review:

- [Bookmark Manager specification](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/spec.md)
- [Quality checklist](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/checklists/requirements.md)

It covers private user accounts, saving and opening bookmarks, tags, favorites, search, filters, editing, archiving, and deletion. Sharing, imports, browser extensions, and page archiving are outside the initial release.

All 16 quality checks passed with no unresolved clarifications.

Please approve the specification or tell me what you’d like changed. Once approved, I’ll create the implementation plan.

Thanks — this reads clearly and covers most of what I had in mind: saving links, tags, favorites, search, filters, editing, archiving, and delete-with-confirmation all look right, and I'm fine leaving sharing, imports, extensions, and page archiving for later.

One thing about the core saving experience doesn't match what I pictured, and it's important enough that I'd like it changed before we move on. When I save a link, I don't want to have to type the title myself every time — the whole point for me is that I paste a web address and the app fills in the page's title (and ideally its description/icon) automatically so saving is quick. The spec makes the title something I must enter and explicitly leaves automatic fetching out. I'd like saving a bookmark from just the address, with the title pulled in for me, to be part of this first release. I should of course still be able to edit that title afterward.

Everything else here is good enough for me. Please update that saving behavior and then we can go to the plan.

content:
The specification now reflects the address-only saving flow:

- Page title is retrieved automatically.
- Description and icon are included when available.
- Retrieval failures still save the bookmark with an address-derived title.
- Users can edit the title, and their edits won’t be overwritten.
- Metadata retrieval is limited to publicly reachable pages.

The revised spec and checklist pass validation:

- [Updated bookmark specification](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/spec.md)
- [Specification quality checklist](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/checklists/requirements.md)

Please confirm the revision, and I’ll move to the implementation plan.

That's exactly what I wanted — I can now save a link just by pasting the address and have the title (plus description and icon when there) filled in for me, edit it if I like, and still get the bookmark saved even when a page can't be reached. This covers the saving experience I had in mind.

The specification looks good to me. Please go ahead and create the implementation plan.

content:
The implementation plan is ready for review:

- [Implementation plan](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/plan.md)
- [Technical research](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/research.md)
- [Data model](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/data-model.md)
- [Application API contract](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/contracts/openapi.yaml)
- [Authentication contract](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/contracts/auth.md)
- [Validation quickstart](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/quickstart.md)

Key choices include a single Next.js 16/Node.js 24 application, Better Auth, SQLite with full-text search, and guarded metadata retrieval with SSRF protection and reliable fallbacks. These choices follow the current [Next.js support policy](https://nextjs.org/support-policy) and [Better Auth’s Next.js/SQLite guidance](https://better-auth.com/docs/installation).

The OpenAPI contract passes validation, all planning clarifications are resolved, and no application code or tasks have been generated yet.

Please approve the plan or request changes. Once approved, I’ll generate the actionable task breakdown.

This all sounds sensible to me. I can't judge the technical choices in detail, but I can see the plan covers the things I care about — private accounts, saving a link from just its address with the title and details fetched safely, searching and filtering, favorites, editing, archiving, and delete-with-confirmation. That's what I approved, so please go ahead and create the task breakdown.

The actionable task breakdown is ready: [tasks.md](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/tasks.md).

It contains:

- 68 sequential tasks
- 17 tasks for saving and revisiting bookmarks
- 11 tasks for search, tags, filters, and favorites
- 9 tasks for editing, archiving, restoration, and deletion
- 31 parallelizable tasks
- Explicit tests and checkpoints for each user story
- MVP scope through T038: private accounts plus address-only bookmark saving and metadata retrieval

All tasks follow the required checkbox, ID, story-label, and file-path format.

Please approve the task breakdown, and I’ll begin implementation.

The task breakdown looks well organized and covers the features I care about — saving from an address with details fetched, search and tags and favorites, and editing, archiving, restoring, and deleting. Please go ahead and begin implementation.

content:
Implementation is complete and ready for review at:

- App: http://maker:4000/bookmarks
- Email: `reviewer@example.com`
- Password: `Review-Bookmark-2026!`

Delivered private accounts, automatic metadata fetching with safe fallback, tags, favorites, search, filters, pagination, editing, archiving/restoring, and confirmed deletion.

Validation passed:

- 37 unit/integration tests
- 9 contract tests
- 14 desktop/mobile browser journeys
- 10,000-bookmark/500-tag performance gate
- Production build, lint, typecheck, and dependency audit

All 68 tasks are complete in [tasks.md](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/tasks.md). Full results are in [validation-results.md](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/validation-results.md), with setup and operations documented in [README.md](/work/README.md).

This is what I was hoping for. The app is up and running, and everything I care about is there: I sign in to my own private library, save a link just by pasting its address with the title and details gathered for me (and a sensible fallback when a page can't be reached), organize with tags and favorites, search and filter to find things again, and edit, archive, restore, or delete with a confirmation. The checks you ran back all of that up, including keeping one account's bookmarks away from another.

I'm happy with this — it does what I set out to build. Accepted.

(For somewhere down the road, not now: it'd be nice to bring in my existing bookmarks from a file and to save whole pages for offline reading. No changes needed today.)
